title: Appeals and Grievances: Days a Decided Medical Necessity Reconsideration Still Covers on an Inpatient Authorization
content:
## Appeals and Grievances — days a decided Medical Necessity Reconsideration still covers

Scope: a second-level reconsideration asked for on a decided Medical Necessity Reconsideration of an inpatient mental health authorization.

**Clause.** The days the case still covers are counted from its decision and the authorization's unit ledger: where the case was decided partially overturned, they are the days requested less the days the authorization granted when first decided and less the days granted on appeal; where the case was decided upheld and extensions were granted on the authorization, they are the days requested less the days first granted and less the extension days granted; in every other case they are the days requested less the days first granted. The count never goes below zero.

**Records read, in Referrals and Authorizations.** On the authorization the case concerns: the units (days) requested and the units authorized when first decided; on its unit ledger, the units granted with the basis "appeal overturn" (days granted on appeal) and the units added by extension (extension days granted). From the case itself: its decision status.

| Case decided | Extensions granted on the authorization | Days still covered |
|---|---|---|
| partially overturned | any | requested less first granted less granted on appeal |
| upheld | yes (more than zero days) | requested less first granted less extension days |
| upheld | no | requested less first granted |
| any other outcome | any | requested less first granted |

**Hypothetical figures** — days requested 14, first granted 7:

- Partially overturned, 3 days granted on appeal: 14 less 7 less 3, which is 4.
- Upheld, 5 extension days granted: 14 less 7 less 5, which is 2.
- Upheld, no extension: 7.
- Partially overturned, 9 days granted on appeal: 14 less 7 less 9 would be negative, so 0.
